title: Composite role graph and scope contracts for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a canonical composable role graph and scope contract for RBAC v2 that supports: project- and tenant-scoped admin roles, fine-grained resource axes (namespace, model, deployment), deterministic conflict resolution, audit-tag propagation, and SSO/SAML attribute translation. The goal is a compact runtime representation that lets the serving runtime and Console enforce permissions consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A clear schema for composite roles that composes atomic role fragments along resource axes (tenant, project, model, route).
Deterministic evaluation order documented and implemented in the role resolver library with unit tests covering inheritance and collisions.
Audit tags (actor_id, role_origin, evaluated_scope, decision_reason) emitted for every allow/deny decision and surfaced in Console traces and retention logs.
SSO/SAML attribute mapping defined with fallback rules and E2E test harness against SAML IdP emulator.
Migration plan to translate existing role assignments to new composite contracts with an opt-in canary path for 5% of customers.
technical_design: We will model roles as ordered tuples: (role_fragment, resource_axis, constraints). A role_fragment is reusable and names a capability (e.g., 'read_cache_kv', 'deploy_model', 'manage_billing'). Resource_axis is one of: global, tenant, project, model, deployment. Constraints are simple attribute checks (e.g., environment==prod). The runtime will flatten composed tuples into an evaluation list sorted by precedence: explicit assignment > role-bound scope > inherited tenant-level > global default. Deny rules always win and carry an explicit denial reason token. The role resolver library exposes a compact encoded blob used by agents (Console / Runtime / CLI) to avoid repeated database lookups.
migration_plan: 1) Export current role assignments and group by tenant and project.
2) Map legacy roles to role_fragments using translation table (run locally and review results).
3) Create composite role objects in write-only mode (no enforcement) and run a shadow evaluation for 2 weeks comparing old vs new decisions.
4) Enable canary enforcement for internal tenants and 5% of external tenants for 1 week.
5) Roll out progressive enforcement in waves, monitor regressions, and provide rollback path to legacy resolver.
rollout_plan: Canary group: internal ops + staging tenants (week 1)
External canary: 5% of eligible customers, opt-in via support toggle (weeks 2-3)
Gradual ramp to 100% based on regression metrics (uptime, permission errors, false-deny rate)
Post-rollout: run reconciliation job to garbage-collect translated role fragments and mark legacy representation for deletion
audit_requirements: Emit allow/deny events to audit-log stream with fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, role_fragments_evaluated, matched_rule_id, decision, decision_reason, resource_path, request_id, session_id, SSO_assertion_id.
Retention: 90 days by default, configurable per-tenant up to 2 years via Console addon.
Immutable append-only storage with HMAC of event payload to detect tampering for Private deployments (customer-provided HSM optional).
Correlation: link eval events to trace IDs used by runtime for per-request latency aggregation.
sso_saml_mapping: Define canonical SAML attribute mapping table: 'eduPersonAffiliation' -> role_hint, 'groups' -> tenant_group, 'employeeNumber' -> external_id. Mapping supports transformation rules (regex capture, prefix/suffix) and explicit deny/allow lists. Fallback: if no role_hint present, fall back to provisioning rules based on SCIM group membership. Tests: SAML emulator with positive/negative cases and signed assertion validation.
